translation: When the front region lies across the cunkou and is round and round (wanwan), it is the Ren vessel; when it moves it causes lower abdominal pain, rebellious qi rushing to the heart, and cramping of the chest with inability to bend and stretch. The Pulse Classic says: When the cunkou pulse is tight, fine, solid, and long, reaching down to the guan, it is the Ren vessel; when it moves it causes lower abdominal pain encircling the navel, in men the seven hernias, in women abdominal masses (jiaju). When all three regions are floating and run straight up and down, it is the Governing Vessel; when it moves it causes stiffness and pain of the lower back and spine, inability to bend and stretch, in adults mania, in children epilepsy.
